coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Prequel Park (interim)
names: Portions of Seawall Lot 349 and Pier 72
record.summary: The interim Prequel Park: about 2 acres per the Port memo (2.5 acres per the Power Station website, 2.75 per press), designed with Heatherwick Studio around Unit 3 and the 300-foot Stack, on the developer-owned Power Station sub-area and on Port-owned shoreline land (portions of Seawall Lot 349 and Pier 72, leased to California Barrel Company for 66 years under Port Lease L-16662), of which about 0.4 acre is on Port property. The Port Commission amended the lease's permitted uses on Nov 18, 2025 (Resolution 25-70); the Port memo of Nov 2025 targets construction in 2026 and opening in 2027, and the project's BCDC amendment was issued June 26, 2026. No source found confirms construction has started.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- Pier & Point's own composition, not a drawn plan: no source read draws Prequel Park's boundary (the Port memo's Exhibit 1 is an unscaled schematic of the ownership sub-areas and the interim improvements; the Power Station website's map page shows an aerial rendering with no outline). The shape is the band of shoreline between Block 9's south edge and Block 4's north edge (each extended to the shore), joined with Block 9, Block 4 and Humboldt Street Plaza, which the interim park is read to occupy until those are built. That makes it 13,876 m2 (3.4 acres). Sources give about 2 acres (Port memo, Calendar Item 10A, Nov 14, 2025), 2.5 acres (Power Station website) and 2.75 acres (press), so none of these figures is certain. It overlaps Block 9, Block 4 and the plaza on purpose, and the overlap ends when those are built.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 (shoreline shown as 'Waterfront Park'); Port Commission memo of Nov 14, 2025 (Calendar Item 10A) for the ~2-acre interim Prequel Park. (An earlier version also cited a Spring 2026 development-forecast listing that could not be located online and is not relied on.)
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own: 92% of the shape lies inside DataSF's active lot 4175028 (21,885 m2, 1241 Delaware St), an undivided lot that also holds Blocks 3, 4 and 9, Humboldt Street Plaza, the Stack and parts of the shoreline parks (checked 2026-10-11).
notes.regulatory_context: The Potrero Power Station-land portion of the ~2-acre Prequel Park interim open-space project (see 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' for the Port-jurisdiction portion and its own sourcing; the Port memo of Nov 14, 2025 puts about 0.4 acre on the Port premises). Per the Port memo the park is to include a multi-purpose lawn and sport courts, amphitheater seating, a quarter-mile walking and running track, water access and restrooms. Construction start is targeted for the third quarter of 2026 per the memo's p.4 (p.2 says the first quarter of 2026); no source confirms a start, so the status is 'planned'.

open_questions: Corrected 2026-09-24: the timeline had shown 'under construction' today but 'planned' a couple of years in the future, because this record's map-shape status ('under construction') had not been updated to match its own sourced finding that no dated source confirms a construction start. The status was changed to 'planned', matching the related 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' record. Still true as of that correction: no dated source confirms construction has started; the latest primary statement is the Port memo (Nov 2025, start Q1 or Q3 2026) and ICA SF ('Construction begins in 2026', Oct 2025).

Area: ~2 acres (Port memo), 2.5 acres (developer site), 2.75 acres (Chronicle, ICA SF), 'almost three' (Potrero View); the BCDC amendment scope is 57,000-62,000 sq ft within the shoreline band only. The developer-land share is not stated anywhere (the ~1.6 acres given on this record's map shape is a subtraction, not a sourced figure).

The 'Spring 2026 SF development pipeline' listing previously cited in this record's map-shape notes (developer FIFTH SPACE; scope demolition, grading, utilities, stormwater, landscaping) could not be found online; no URL is recorded, and the map-shape notes no longer rely on it (2026-09-29).

BCDC 2019.006.02: received June 19, 2025, issued June 26, 2026 per the BCDC tracker (Pier & Point's map notes and timeline had recorded June 19, 2025 as the issue date; corrected 2026-09-29). The amendment text itself was not found.

Whether the 2024 annual report's 'Delaware East Park/Stack Plaza' temporary activation (Andrea Cochran Landscape Architecture, schematic design from Aug 2024) is the same scheme later branded Prequel Park with Heatherwick Studio is not stated by any source.

Application filing: Chronicle (May 22, 2025) says the application was expected to be filed 'on Thursday'; SF YIMBY (Oct 2025) says 'In May, the developer submitted plans'. No Planning case number found.
Cost: only the developer's own $15-20 million estimate (Chronicle, Potrero View). No construction contract or permit valuation found.

BOS File 260724 (Amended and Restated DA, noticed Sept 11, 2026) amends the Phasing Plan; whether it changes hotel or interim-park obligations is not stated in the legislative digest, and the draft DA text was not read.

Has Prequel Park construction started, and has the 2026 start been rescheduled? As of 2026-10-10 no source read reports a groundbreaking or a new start date; the developer's site still describes the park without reporting construction, and the BCDC permit tracker shows only the June 26, 2026 issuance of Non-Material Amendment 2019.006.02.

BCDC amendment 2019.006.02: this record's mapping notes and timeline said it was 'issued June 19, 2025' (corrected 2026-09-29). The BCDC permit tracker gives June 19, 2025 as the date the application was RECEIVED and June 26, 2026 as the date ISSUED. The amendment document itself was not found on bcdc.ca.gov (2018-2019 DRB/Commission URLs now return 404; the tracker is an embedded table that could not be saved as text). Treat 2025-06-19 as application date, 2026-06-26 as issuance.

Port memo 10A is internally inconsistent: p.2 says construction start Q1 2026 / opening Q1 2027; p.4 says Q3 2026 / Q3 2027. Both are recorded; the p.4 dates follow the DBI-submittal sentence and are the more detailed statement.

No dated source confirms that Prequel Park construction has started as of 2026-09-17 (searched sfport.com, sfplanning.org, Chronicle, SF YIMBY, Potrero View, SF Standard, developer site, ICA SF). This record's map data marks the Power Station sub-area half as under construction without a source.

The 'Spring 2026 SF development pipeline' listing ('Potrero Power Station - Prequel Park', developer FIFTH SPACE, scope demolition/grading/utilities/stormwater/landscaping) cited in this record's mapping notes could not be located online; no URL is on file.
Lease commencement date and the recorded lease are not in the corpus; 'March 2087' implies a ~March 2021 start but no source states it.
Exact footprint of the ~0.4 acre on Port land: memo Exhibit 1 is an unscaled rendering; not digitized.

Whether the 2024 annual report's 'temporary activation east of Delaware Street and Stack Plaza' (Andrea Cochran Landscape Architecture, construction then expected Q1 2026) is the same project later branded Prequel Park with Heatherwick Studio is not stated by any source.
Planning temporary use authorization (June 2025): no case number or document found on sfplanning.org.

Port Commission minutes of Nov 18, 2025: item 10A passed on consent with no discussion or public comment; the minutes URL is https://www.sfport.com/media/10953/download?inline (the meeting page's 'm11182025.pdf' link returns 'page not found').

Area of the whole interim park differs by source: ~2 acres (Port memo), 2.5 acres (developer site), 2.75 acres (Chronicle, ICA SF), 'almost three' (Potrero View); BCDC scope 57,000-62,000 sq ft. Recorded separately; not reconciled.

No source read draws Prequel Park's boundary. The Port memo's Exhibit 1 is an unscaled schematic of the Power Station and Port sub-areas and the interim improvements, and the Power Station website's map page is an aerial rendering with no outline, so the shape on the map is Pier & Point's own composition.

The sources disagree on the park's size: about 2 acres (Port memo, Calendar Item 10A), 2.5 acres (Power Station website) and 2.75 acres (press). The shape on the map is larger (about 3.4 acres) because it includes the ground of Blocks 4 and 9 and Humboldt Street Plaza, which the interim park is read to occupy until they are built.

When the interim park ends is not stated. The Port memo says it would operate Thursday through Sunday 'for a period of at least five years beginning in 2027'; no source gives a closing date or says what replaces it on each parcel.
